questions.q: What is the post mainly about?
options: Humorous observations from living with a two-year-old
A guide to choosing the best toddler books to read aloud
Advice on managing sleep and feeding with a newborn
Why raising a second child is easier than the first
questions.explain: The author reports discoveries about toddlers, such as that they are both boring and brilliant.

questions.q: What did the toddler say that hinted her father should leave her alone while she played with Legos?
options: "Daddy is 43 years old now, right?"
"Daddy needs to work in his office?"
"Can you get out of space?"
"I am so perfectly sad, Daddy"
questions.explain: She said 'Daddy needs to work in his office?' as an unsubtle hint.

questions.q: Why does the daughter say "would you like a strawberry?" when she wants one?
options: She is copying her mother's way of asking
She is trying to be polite when she asks
She thinks "you" is another word for her name
She cannot yet pronounce the word strawberry
questions.explain: Because adults say 'you' to her, she thinks it is a synonym for her name.

questions.q: What phrase did the parents teach the toddler to say when she falls over?
options: Oh no
Kerplunk
I am so perfectly sad
Mamma mia
questions.explain: They taught her to say 'mamma mia' whenever she falls over.

questions.q: What does the author suggest about parenting near the end?
options: Strict rules matter most in shaping a toddler's character
Parenting matters less than we think, so help kids be themselves
Parents should avoid reading the same books to toddlers
Most strong parenting opinions are correct and should be followed
questions.explain: He says parenting probably matters less than we think and we should guide kids toward their best selves.
